trial.title: Study of Tovorafenib in High-Grade Glioma and Diffuse Intrinsic Pontine Glioma (DIPG)
indication: High Grade Glioma (HGG) of the Brain With BRAF Aberration

endpoints.description: Estimate the progression-free survival (PFS) distribution for pediatric and young adult patients (age: ≥12 months and ≤39 years) with newly-diagnosed BRAFV600 mutant HGG (Stratum A) who receive tovorafenib monotherapy post RT compared to molecularly-stratified, matched historical controls.

Estimate the overall survival (OS) distribution for pediatric and young adult patients with newly-diagnosed BRAFV600 mutant HGG (Stratum A) who receive tovorafenib post RT compared to molecularly-stratified, matched historical controls.
Describe OS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with DIPG or DMG harboring MAPK pathway alterations who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).
Describe PFS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with HGG harboring MAPK alterations not included in Stratum A who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).
Describe the OS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with primary spinal cord HGG harboring a MAPK alteration who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).

endpoints.measure: Establish the RP2D of tovorafenib - Stratum C
endpoints.time_frame: At the end of Cycle 1 (each cycle is 28 days)
endpoints.description: Evaluate the feasibility of administration of tovorafenib post craniospinal RT in pediatric and young adult patients with newly diagnosed, metastatic HGG harboring a MAPK alteration (Stratum C).
Describe OS for pediatric and young adult patients with newly-diagnosed, metastatic HGG who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum C).

Evaluate the radiographic objective response rate (ORR \[complete response (CR) + partial response (PR)\]) to tovorafenib treatment post RT in pediatric and young adult patients with newly diagnosed HGG and DIPG/DMG that harbor MAPK alterations (all Strata).

endpoints.measure: Number of participants with tovorafenib-related adverse events as assessed by CTCAE v5.0
endpoints.time_frame: From Day 1 of protocol treatment through 30 days following end of protocol treatment
endpoints.description: Assess and further characterize the safety and toxicity of post-RT tovorafenib in pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with HGG, including DIPG. This will be achieved by calculating the number of participants with, as well as frequency and severity of, tovorafenib-related Adverse Events as assessed by CTCAE v5.0.

endpoints.measure: Correlation between genomic status, recurrence, radiographic response
endpoints.description: Explore longitudinal associations of genomic, transcriptomic, epigenetic, and/or immunologic alterations of tumor at diagnosis, recurrence, or autopsy with radiographic response, advanced neuro-imaging measures, and patient-reported outcomes.

endpoints.measure: Evaluate Health-Related Quality of Life Outcomes
endpoints.description: Evaluate health-related quality of life outcomes of pediatric and young adult patients newly-diagnosed with HGG, including DIPG, treated with tovorafenib, by patient and/or parent reporting at key timepoints in therapy using the patient reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) survey which will be completed by consenting participants every other cycle for the length of their treatment (all Strata).
Describe the PFS for pediatric and young adult patients newly diagnosed with primary spinal cord HGG harboring a MAPK alteration who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum B).
Describe PFS for pediatric and young adult patients with newly-diagnosed, metastatic HGG who receive tovorafenib post RT (Stratum C).

outcome.rationale: Trial tests tovorafenib in challenging HGG/DIPG population with three distinct strata. Stratum A (BRAFV600 HGG) has best supporting evidence from dabrafenib+trametinib data. Stratum B (DIPG) and Stratum C (metastatic) have poor historical outcomes with limited precedent for targeted therapy benefit. Primary endpoint success uncertain given lack of tovorafenib-specific HGG data and post-RT setting. Safety profile expected manageable based on FIREFLY-1 experience.

value.estimand: Pediatric/young adult patients with newly diagnosed BRAFV600 mutant HGG (Stratum A) receiving tovorafenib post-RT vs molecularly-stratified historical controls
value.uncertainty: No direct data for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG; extrapolated from dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed/refractory HGG (median PFS 9 months) and tovorafenib in relapsed LGG. Historical controls for pediatric BRAFV600 HGG have median PFS ~6-9 months post-RT.
value.rationale: Based on dabrafenib+trametinib data in relapsed/refractory BRAFV600 pediatric HGG showing median PFS 9.0 months, tovorafenib as single-agent may achieve similar or modestly improved PFS vs historical controls (median ~6-9 months). However, this is newly diagnosed post-RT setting, not relapsed disease, creating uncertainty.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT07206849 is a Phase 2 study of tovorafenib in pediatric/young adult patients with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma (HGG) including DIPG, with MAPK pathway alterations. Three strata: A (localized BRAFV600 mutant HGG), B (DIPG/DMG or other MAPK-altered HGG), C (metastatic HGG).
Tovorafenib is a type II RAF inhibitor approved (April 2024) for relapsed/refractory pediatric low-grade glioma with BRAF alterations based on FIREFLY-1 trial showing 67% ORR and manageable safety.

Evidence for HGG: Dabrafenib+trametinib in relapsed/refractory BRAFV600-mutant pediatric HGG showed ORR 56.1%, median PFS 9.0 months, median OS 15.0 months (JCO 2023). This provides indirect evidence for MAPK inhibition in pediatric HGG.

Stratum A (BRAFV600 localized HGG): Most comparable to dabrafenib+trametinib data. Predicted ORR ~40-50%, median PFS 8-12 months, median OS 15-20 months vs historical controls (median OS ~12-15 months for pediatric HGG).

Stratum B (DIPG): DIPG has dismal prognosis (median OS <12 months). MAPK alterations in ~10-15% of DIPG. Limited data on targeted therapy efficacy in DIPG specifically. Predicted limited benefit, median OS likely <15 months.
Stratum C (metastatic HGG): Poor prognosis stratum. RP2D feasibility expected to be established (dose escalation/de-escalation design). OS likely poor given metastatic disease.
Safety: Tovorafenib shows manageable toxicity in FIREFLY-1 (rash, hair color change, fatigue). CTCAE Grade 3+ AEs expected in ~20-30% of patients.

Key uncertainties: (1) No direct data for tovorafenib in newly diagnosed HGG (only relapsed/refractory LGG); (2) Post-RT timing (28-35 days) may affect tolerability; (3) DIPG stratum has no validated targeted therapy precedent; (4) Metastatic HGG data extremely limited.

Evidence gaps: No published results for NCT07206849 (not yet recruiting as of knowledge cutoff). All predictions based on indirect evidence from related populations (relapsed LGG, relapsed HGG with BRAF inhibitors).
Endpoint classification: Primary endpoint (PFS Stratum A) is time-to-event with historical comparison. Secondary endpoints include OS (all strata), ORR, safety, and exploratory biomarker analyses.
